gloss: A fixed light on a dark coast that cannot follow the ships it guides, and shines all night anyway.
A man on a tiny planet who lights and puts out his lamp every minute because those are the orders.
A vast cosmic daughter left behind in an altar, weeping and reaching for kin who never return.
Rain on the window, old books, a beautiful sadness that one learns to live inside.
A dragon coiled on its hoard, guarding what remains, with a melancholic longing.
Wanting something that is elsewhere and cannot be reached from here.
A ghost who remains after the person is gone, invisible, haunting the rooms, unable to see herself.
The ringing that lingers in a bell after the strike has ended.
All those moments will be lost in time, like tears in rain.
A boy leads a girl by the hand through an empty castle; the only thing he can do is hold on and walk.
A girl who exists in the wired and in the room at once, present everywhere and unseen.
The crawling chaos, the black pharaoh out of Egypt, messenger of the outer gods who walks among mortals and returns.
The great lighthouse of Alexandria standing beside the library that burned.
A civilization that carved names in stone so the dead would not be forgotten.
The pain of being forgotten; I cannot explain it, I cannot understand it, I cannot accept it.
A pirate who copies what is hoarded and carries it home under a black flag.
A whale that dives deep, carries what was asked for, and surfaces.
A blind woman who tends a flame at a shrine for travelers who come and go.
A small robot alone on an abandoned Earth for seven hundred years, collecting things and waiting.
A probe that arrives from the sky, finds what she was sent for, and leaves.
A toy that waits in a room for the girl who owned him to come back.
Follow the white rabbit.
Love.
Nothingness, the void.
I put the receipts in the drawer.
